punchline: Kabat-Zinn took the title of his book from a joke in the 1964 film Zorba the Greek.
thirty_sec: On a boat to Crete, Basil asks Zorba whether he is married. Zorba lists wife, children, house, everything, and calls it the full catastrophe. Jon Kabat-Zinn made it the title of his book. His editor feared the word catastrophe would repel readers, but the phrase kept coming back to him. He reads it as an affirmation of life's chaos, to be embraced and not lamented.
